stem:
A GP reviews a 64-year-old with new abdominal bloating and early satiety. Ultrasound shows a 6.5-cm multilocular adnexal mass with solid papillary projections and ascites. CA125 is 28 U/mL (local reference <35). She is haemodynamically stable, without acute pain.

Which next step best fits the combined findings?

options.label: A
options.text: Repeat pelvic ultrasound in six weeks to assess for resolution
options.explanation: Functional cysts that resolve are a premenopausal phenomenon; a multilocular mass with solid papillary projections and ascites at 64 is not expected to resolve.

options.label: B
options.text: Refer to a general gynaecologist for laparoscopic cystectomy
options.explanation: Laparoscopic cystectomy outside a cancer service risks rupture and inadequate staging of a probable malignancy.

options.label: C
options.text: Refer promptly to a gynaecological oncology service
options.explanation: Solid papillary projections, multilocularity and ascites give a high risk-of-malignancy score (above 200) even with a CA125 of 28, so she needs prompt gynaecological oncology care.

options.label: D
options.text: Arrange HE4 and CEA, referring only if either is raised
options.explanation: Additional markers do not override high-risk morphology and would only delay referral.

options.label: E
options.text: Repeat CA125 in four weeks and refer if it rises above 35
options.explanation: CA125 is normal in a substantial proportion of early ovarian cancers; waiting for it to rise delays treatment.

context: Suspicious postmenopausal adnexal imaging warrants cancer-service assessment even when CA125 is within the stated laboratory range.
